meta.name: AI Papers
meta.desc: A prioritized paper library for AI engineers: foundations, post-training, reasoning, agents, retrieval, serving, and evaluation.
meta.selectionNote: Must-read, core, and very useful papers form the main path; selected sections and optional papers are supplemental. Links point to primary arXiv records.

categories.name: Architecture & Scaling
categories.desc: Start here: transformer mechanics, in-context learning, compute-aware scaling, and a modern end-to-end model stack.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.why: Introduces the Transformer architecture that underpins modern LLMs.

papers.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
papers.why: Read the abstract, Sections 1–3, and limitations rather than every appendix; it establishes in-context learning as an LLM interface.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.why: Historically important scaling intuition; optional once you have read Chinchilla carefully.

papers.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
papers.why: Revises the scaling recipe and shows why training tokens must grow with model size.

papers.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
papers.why: A modern, unusually complete account of data, pretraining, post-training, safety, evaluation, and production model design.

papers.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
papers.why: A dense modern blueprint for efficient large-scale training: MoE, MLA, auxiliary-loss-free load balancing, multi-token prediction, and FP8.

papers.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
papers.why: A practical account of unified thinking and non-thinking modes, reasoning budgets, MoE variants, multilingual training, and distillation.

papers.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
papers.why: Connects a one-trillion-parameter MoE, the MuonClip optimizer, agentic data synthesis, and environment-based reinforcement learning.

categories.name: Adaptation & Alignment
categories.desc: How base models become useful assistants, and how to adapt them without retraining every parameter.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
papers.why: The clearest end-to-end account of supervised instruction tuning, reward modeling, and RLHF.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.why: Introduces the parameter-efficient adapter technique used throughout practical LLM fine-tuning.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.why: Combines quantization and LoRA to make high-quality fine-tuning possible on far less memory.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.why: Derives a simpler preference-training objective that avoids a separate reward model and online RL loop.

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.why: Connects reinforcement learning, cold-start data, distillation, and the emergence of reasoning behavior in a modern model family.

papers.title: s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
papers.why: A clean bridge from standard LLMs to reasoning models, showing how budget forcing and extra inference-time compute affect performance.

categories.name: Prompting, Reasoning & Agents
categories.desc: The ideas behind deliberate reasoning, tool loops, and agents that can interact with external systems.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.why: Demonstrates how intermediate reasoning examples can unlock multi-step problem solving.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.why: Provides the core reason-act-observe loop used by many production agent systems.

papers.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
papers.why: Shows that an agent's tools and interface design can matter as much as its prompt or base model.

papers.title: τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
papers.why: Tests production-like coordination where both the user and agent use tools to change shared state, exposing reasoning and communication failures.

categories.name: Retrieval & Long Context
categories.desc: The retrieval stack behind grounded applications, plus the failure modes that matter in production.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.why: Introduces the canonical architecture for combining parametric models with retrievable knowledge.

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.why: Shows that a large context window does not guarantee reliable use of information throughout that window.

papers.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.why: Explores adaptive retrieval and self-critique instead of blindly retrieving a fixed number of chunks.

papers.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.why: Separates retrieval quality, faithfulness, and answer quality into practical reference-free RAG metrics.

papers.title: Long Context vs. RAG for LLMs: An Evaluation and Revisits
papers.why: Directly compares long-context prompting with retrieval and clarifies when each approach wins across different query and corpus types.

papers.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
papers.why: Useful for enterprise corpora that need global sensemaking through entity graphs, communities, and hierarchical summaries.

categories.name: Serving & Evaluation
categories.desc: The systems ideas that make LLM applications fast and affordable, and the evaluation discipline that keeps them honest.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.why: Shows why memory movement, not just FLOPs, determines real attention performance on GPUs.

papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
papers.why: Explains vLLM's KV-cache paging design and the throughput mechanics of modern LLM serving.

papers.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
papers.why: Introduces scalable LLM-based evaluation while making position, verbosity, self-enhancement, and reasoning biases explicit.

papers.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
papers.why: Historically important framework for evaluation across scenarios, metrics, risks, and tradeoffs; optional after modern application-eval papers.
